# Supported format profiles

<!-- Generated by tools/formats/check.py --write; edit crates/aa-core/src/formats.json. -->

This catalogue tracks **29 primary input-format families + 4 compression formats = 33 entries**, and **11 declaration families** tracked separately.

Count implemented primary families and compression formats, merging aliases and variants. Declaration families and nested structures are separate. Implementation counts are not universal format or platform qualification claims.

The declaration list is maintained separately from primary inputs and nested structures.
Each row describes a bounded profile. Evidence links identify implementations and
existing scope records; they do not establish every variant or platform was tested.
See [limitations](LIMITATIONS.md) for qualification boundaries. Planned entries
contribute nothing to the implementation total. HTML/PDF/JSON report outputs,
directory workflows and nested metadata structures are not primary input families.

The same catalogue is available offline as `analyze-anything formats --json`.

| SquashFS | primary | squashfs | Little-endian SquashFS v4.0 gzip/XZ metadata, ordinary file bytes, ID/fragment tables and link declarations, read without mounting. [record 1](../crates/aa-linux/src/squashfs.rs) [record 2](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/SQUASHFS.md) [record 3](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/upstream-hello-world-29.snap) [record 4](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/squashfs-native.ref.json) [record 5](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/appimage-external.ref.json) [record 6](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/linux-images-native.ref.json) | Only gzip/XZ: 8 KiB metadata and 1 MiB data blocks, 16 MiB decoded metadata/fragment cache, 256 MiB per file and 512 MiB shared data decoding; XZ decoder memory is capped at 32 MiB. Recorded real samples cover Canonical hello-world 29 (XZ) and external AppImageKit 12 (gzip); fragment and broader inode/compressor combinations retain constructed or pending native qualification. Links, special files, xattrs/ACL effects, export lookup and runtime behavior remain declarations or explicit gaps. Other filesystem versions and compressors are unsupported. |
| AppImage Type 2 | primary | AppImage | Type 2 ELF runtime/image boundaries, captured SquashFS contents, root Desktop Entry identity and bounded literal AppRun-to-supplied-file evidence. [record 1](../crates/aa-linux/src/appimage.rs) [record 2](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/APPIMAGE-SNAP.md) [record 3](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/appimage-external.ref.json) [record 4](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/linux-images-native.ref.json) | Ordinary ELF section tables only, capped at 8192 sections and 1024 program headers; Type 1, absent/extended section counts and unsupported layouts remain unread. The pinned external AppImageKit 12 ELF64 little-endian/gzip image has 135 Windows 7-Zip checks and 62 Linux unsquashfs checks at a600591; other ELF classes/byte orders retain constructed tests only. No runtime invocation or mounting. AppRun matching excludes absolute/escaping links, multiple hops, renamed/ambiguous targets and incomplete namespaces; relationships share a 16 MiB output budget. Desktop Entry Version does not establish a software release version. |
| snap package | primary | snap | Canonical captured meta/snap.yaml identity, application/interface/daemon/environment/hook declarations and bounded supplied-file command/hook evidence over SquashFS. [record 1](../crates/aa-linux/src/snap.rs) [record 2](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/APPIMAGE-SNAP.md) [record 3](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/upstream-hello-world-29.snap) [record 4](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/squashfs-native.ref.json) [record 5](../crates/aa-linux/tests/data/linux-images-native.ref.json) | Metadata is capped at 256 KiB per file, 16 MiB aggregate, 12000 YAML events and depth 24; duplicates, aliases, anchors, tags, merge keys and multiple documents are rejected. Canonical hello-world 6.4 revision 29 exercises identity and four supplied application targets, with 22 Linux unsquashfs checks at a600591; other schemas and runtime profiles are not universally qualified. Literal commands and observed hooks are evidence, not execution. No store/signature verification, installation, confinement enforcement, host lookup or symlink following; supplied-target output shares a 16 MiB budget. |

## Planned profiles

| Family | Group | Aliases | Scope and evidence | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Python wheel | primary | whl | Wheel identity, dependency/entry-point metadata and captured distribution contents. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
| npm package tarball | primary | npm tgz | Package identity, dependencies, literal lifecycle scripts and captured component contents. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
| Java archive family | primary | jar, war, ear | Start with a qualified JAR manifest/entry/dependency profile; WAR/EAR require separate profile qualification. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
| Alpine Linux package | primary | Alpine apk | Explicitly qualified Alpine package metadata, payload and signature-declaration profiles. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
| Flatpak single-file bundle | primary | flatpak | Bounded OSTree-backed application-bundle structures and captured object relationships. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
| OCI/Docker image family | primary | OCI image layout, docker-save archive | Bounded image manifests, ordered layers, whiteout declarations and digest/source relationships. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
| LZ4 framed stream | compression | lz4 | Bounded LZ4 framed decoding; raw blocks are a separate unsupported profile. | Not implemented or included in the supported total. |
